sb_spends.effect: He summons shades of those who broke promises to him.

Cinder-Wyrm (Dragon's Lair).summary: A young dragon-kin that nests in volcanic ash and feeds on ember-rich ore. Possesses a cunning intelligence and a territorial fury.
Cinder-Wyrm (Dragon's Lair).lore: The cinder-wyrms are the children of Azghal the Doomfire, born from the molten gates of his Red Vault. They serve as his eyes and his enforcers, and they remember every face that has ever offered tribute to their sire.

sb_spends.name: [FIRE] Scatter embers
sb_spends.effect: It shakes ash and embers, igniting flammable surfaces.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Forge heat builds
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Furnace' timer. At 4, the chamber becomes unbearably hot.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Demand tribute
sb_spends.effect: It pauses to accept tribute; refusal enrages it.

Hoard-Wyrd (Dragon's Lair).summary: A ghost bonded to a specific treasure. It permits those who swear an oath to borrow its relic—but it always remembers the terms.
Hoard-Wyrd (Dragon's Lair).lore: A wyrd does not guard the hoard; it is the hoard's memory made manifest. It does not sleep. It does not forget. It counts the days since the treasure was taken, and it will ask for its return—or for the story of its journey.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] State the terms
sb_spends.effect: It names the oath required to borrow the relic.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Debt comes due
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Debt' timer. At 4, the borrower must return the relic or face a geas.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Remind of the oath
sb_spends.effect: It whispers the terms to a PC, causing them to lose a Boon if they have broken them.

Sky-Needle Wyvern (Dragon's Lair).summary: A wyvern that nests on the highest peaks, hunting updrafts and snatching prey from sheer cliffs.
Sky-Needle Wyvern (Dragon's Lair).lore: The wyverns of the Sky Needles are the children of Tyrgoth the Thunder-Eater. They challenge travelers who climb too high—not to kill, but to test their worth. Those who pass may claim a feather.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Snatch and drop
sb_spends.effect: It grabs a PC and drops them toward the cliff.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Test of worth
sb_spends.effect: It challenges a PC to stand firm against the wind; failure means being knocked Prone.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Tyrgoth watches
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Thunder-Eater's Eye' timer. At 4, Tyrgoth notices the climbers.

Frostling Wyrm (Dragon's Lair).summary: A small but cunning wyrm that breathes rime and seals doors with ice-ribbing. Dwells in glacier cathedrals.
Frostling Wyrm (Dragon's Lair).lore: The frostling wyrm is the child of Vyrmja the Winter Coil. It does not attack with rage—it hunts with patience, freezing the ground beneath its prey and waiting for the cold to do its work.

sb_spends.name: [ICE] Seal the door
sb_spends.effect: It ices over an exit, sealing it shut.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Cold takes hold
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Deep Freeze' timer. At 4, all in Near take Harm from cold.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Ice underfoot
sb_spends.effect: It freezes the ground; movement becomes Desperate.

Lampwyrm Archivist (Dragon's Lair).summary: A drake that hoards knowledge, not gold. It illuminates lies and hums lullabies of forgotten history.
Lampwyrm Archivist (Dragon's Lair).lore: The lampwyrm was once a servant of the Lethai-thora, tasked with guarding forbidden knowledge. It still remembers the old protocols—and it still enforces them.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Illuminate a lie
sb_spends.effect: Its light reveals a lie a PC has told.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Knowledge for silence
sb_spends.effect: It offers a forbidden fact if the party swears never to speak it.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Protocols engage
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Archive Seals' timer. At 4, the archive locks down.

The Worn (Malachai).summary: A hollowed shell of a former mortal who accepted Malachai's curse and succumbed completely. Still speaks, still begs—but the hunger is all that remains.
The Worn (Malachai).lore: The Worn were once vampires, werewolves, slashers, or memory-eaters who gave in to their appetites. They are drawn back to the cursed city, where they wander the salt flats and whisper the names of those who still have hope—and who still have time.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Beg for release
sb_spends.effect: It begs a PC to end it; hesitation costs a Boon.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Whisper a name
sb_spends.effect: It whispers the name of someone the PC loves who is in danger.

sb_spends.name: [CURSE] Spread the hunger
sb_spends.effect: Its touch reminds a PC of their own appetites; they mark Fatigue.

The Slasher (Unkillable Killer).summary: An immortal killer who cannot die, driven by a hunger for violence that grows with each life taken.
The Slasher (Unkillable Killer).lore: The slasher was once a soldier who begged Malachai for vengeance. She answered—but the price was eternal, and the hunger can never be fed. Their face appears in every mirror, watching.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Stalk in the mirror
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Stalk' timer. At 4, the Slasher appears in a reflection and strikes.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Face in the glass
sb_spends.effect: A PC sees the Slasher's face in every reflective surface.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Trail of bodies
sb_spends.effect: It leaves corpses that rise as The Worn to harry the party.

The Slasher (Unkillable Killer).harm_levels: 8 (advanced); only silver, fire, or a rite at the first victim's grave counts against this pool.

Memory Eater (Psychic Vampire).summary: A creature that feeds on fresh memories, stealing the past to fuel its own endless hunger.
Memory Eater (Psychic Vampire).lore: The memory eaters were once scholars, spies, or lovers who wanted to preserve what they could not keep. Now they consume the past of others, leaving only hollow gaps where love and fear once lived.

sb_spends.name: [MEMORY] Steal a recent memory
sb_spends.effect: It consumes a recent memory from a PC.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Return for a deeper memory
sb_spends.effect: It offers to return the stolen memory for an older, dearer one.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Hollow gaps spread
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Hollowing' timer. At 4, a PC forgets a bond or talent.

The Changeling (Faceless).summary: A creature that can change appearance at will, but in doing so forgets who it was originally.
The Changeling (Faceless).lore: The changeling was once a person who wanted to escape their past. Malachai offered them a new face—and then another, and another, until the original was lost entirely.

sb_spends.name: [ILLUSION] New face
sb_spends.effect: It assumes a new appearance mid-combat, confusing targeting.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Wear a PC's face
sb_spends.effect: It takes a PC's face, sowing distrust among allies.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Offer escape from self
sb_spends.effect: It offers a PC a new identity in exchange for their old name.

The Plague Bearer (Contagion).summary: A healer who took a plague into themselves, now a walking blight. They are immune to disease—but they carry every disease they have touched.
The Plague Bearer (Contagion).lore: The plague bearer wanted to save their people. Malachai gave them the power to absorb any sickness—but the sickness lives inside them still, and it will not be denied forever.

sb_spends.name: [CURSE] Infection spreads
sb_spends.effect: A PC is exposed; start a 4-segment 'Infection' timer.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Outbreak
sb_spends.effect: Start a 6-segment 'Outbreak' timer. At 6, the disease becomes contagious in the region.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Absorb another's sickness
sb_spends.effect: It offers to take a PC's disease, but must give one back.

Lamp-Eater (Moira's Journals).summary: A large, nocturnal omnivore that follows bioluminescent fungi and sources of light. Confused, not aggressive—but dangerous when frustrated.
Lamp-Eater (Moira's Journals).lore: The lamp-eater feeds on glow-fungus, but it has learned that travelers carry light—and sometimes, that light is edible. It follows lanterns, hoping to feast. When it cannot, it grows angry.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Eat the light
sb_spends.effect: It devours a light source, plunging the area into darkness.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Offer glow-fungus
sb_spends.effect: Offering glow-fungus distracts it.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Frustration builds
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Frustrated' timer. At 4, it rampages.

Hedge-Crawler (Moira's Journals).summary: A many-legged insect that nests in old oaks. It emerges at dusk, forming slow-moving columns that stain anything they touch.
Hedge-Crawler (Moira's Journals).lore: The hedge-crawler is not dangerous, but it is persistent. Its oil stains skin for days and attracts scavengers. The Aelaerem say it was once a border-marking spirit that forgot its purpose.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Oil stain
sb_spends.effect: Its oil marks a PC, attracting predators.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Column grows
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Swarm' timer. At 4, the column becomes difficult terrain.

Pressure Eel (Moira's Journals).summary: A translucent creature that slides through cracks in stone, triggering old mechanisms with its passage.
Pressure Eel (Moira's Journals).lore: The pressure eel is a remnant of the Astroegro's living infrastructure. It does not attack—it simply moves, and in moving, it wakes what should sleep.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Trigger a mechanism
sb_spends.effect: Its passage activates a trap or opens a sealed door.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Wake the dungeon
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Dungeon Wakes' timer. At 4, dormant defenses activate.

Thread-Bird (Fairy Warbler).summary: A finch-sized bird with red thread-like markings. It follows travelers and mimics human speech patterns.
Thread-Bird (Fairy Warbler).lore: The thread-birds are said to carry messages between the living and the Neighbors. They do not speak with intent—they mimic what they hear, and their warnings are echoes, not advice.

sb_spends.name: [FEY] Mimic a secret
sb_spends.effect: It mimics something private a PC once said, revealing it to others.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Neighbors listen
sb_spends.effect: Its chirping alerts the Neighbors to the party's presence.

Dream-Eater (Narethi).summary: A jackal-like spirit with too many eyes, born from the Unburied's hunger. It does not kill—it collects memories.
Dream-Eater (Narethi).lore: The dream-eater is not a predator in the ordinary sense. It takes what the Unburied has demanded: a name, a face, a moment of warmth. Those who lose to it remember the fact of their loss, but not the feeling.

sb_spends.name: [DREAM] Take a dream
sb_spends.effect: It consumes a dream from a sleeping PC.

sb_spends.name: [MEMORY] Claim a face
sb_spends.effect: It steals the memory of a face; a PC cannot recall someone they love.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Trade memory for memory
sb_spends.effect: It offers to return a taken memory for one the PC has not yet lost.

Watcher (Narethi).summary: A priest-archivist who maintains the Bone Archive and tends the Unburied's sleep. Their face is hidden behind a salt-cured mask.
Watcher (Narethi).lore: The Watchers are the memory of the Narethi people. They tattoo the names of the dead onto their own skin, and they speak only when the ancestors demand it.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Record your words
sb_spends.effect: The Watcher writes down a PC's words; they are now part of the Archive.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Archive access
sb_spends.effect: It offers access to forbidden records in exchange for a name.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] The ancestors stir
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Ancestral Voice' timer. At 4, the dead demand answers.

Unbound Exile (Narethi).summary: A Narethi who chose the Riven Path over Stillness, now wandering the desert and selling psionic services to survive.
Unbound Exile (Narethi).lore: The Unbound are exiles not because they are dangerous, but because they are honest. They admit that the Unburied's dream is not a curse—it is an inheritance, and they will claim it.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Psionic service
sb_spends.effect: It offers a psychic service for a favor or secret.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Uncomfortable truth
sb_spends.effect: It speaks a truth the party does not want to hear.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Riven path opens
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Riven Path' timer. At 4, it demonstrates the Unburied's power.

Bone-Scribe (Narethi).summary: An archivist who records the names of the dead on bone with needles dipped in their own blood.
Bone-Scribe (Narethi).lore: A Bone-Scribe does not speak. Their voice is the scratch of needle on bone, and their memory is the Archive itself. They recall every name that has ever been recorded—and they do not forgive.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Inscribe a name
sb_spends.effect: It begins writing a PC's name in bone; the PC is bound to a promise.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Erase a name
sb_spends.effect: It offers to erase a name from the Archive for a terrible price.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Scratch of needle
sb_spends.effect: The sound of its needle unsettles all in Near; they lose a Boon.

Ghost Herd (Kuvani/Narethi).summary: A herd of spectral horses that rides the salt pan on moonless nights, seeking a battle that will never come.
Ghost Herd (Kuvani/Narethi).lore: The ghost herd is said to be the souls of warriors who died without honor. They ride forever—and sometimes, when the Hollow is close, they ride through the waking world.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Ride through
sb_spends.effect: The herd charges through the party; all must test Spirit or panic.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Endless ride
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Ride' timer. At 4, a PC is swept up and carried into the Hollow.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Test of honor
sb_spends.effect: They challenge a PC to name an honorable deed; failure draws their wrath.

The Unburied (Narethi Myth).summary: The mummified First One sealed beneath the Sunken Courts. It does not speak—it dreams, and its dreams leak into the world.
locations: The Heart of the Deep Desert
The Unburied (Narethi Myth).lore: The Unburied was once a sorcerer-king who reached into a well of power and pulled something back. It did not die—it transformed into a dream made flesh, and that dream is the Narethi's curse and their inheritance.

sb_spends.name: [DREAM] Dream leaks
sb_spends.effect: Its dream spills into reality; all PCs see visions of their failures.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Awakening
sb_spends.effect: Start an 8-segment 'Awakening' timer. At 8, the Unburied fully wakes.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Dreams made flesh
sb_spends.effect: Its dream births nightmare creatures to defend it.

The Covenant Child.summary: A child with silver wire eyes, sent to enforce broken covenants. It does not speak—it waits, and its patience is absolute.
The Covenant Child.lore: The Covenant Child serves both Malachai and the Daughters of the Unbroken Cord. It does not care which master it answers to—it only cares that the promise is kept.
connections: The Daughters of the Unbroken Cord

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Name the price
sb_spends.effect: It holds out its hand, demanding the price of the broken covenant.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Debt comes due
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Debt' timer. At 4, the breaker suffers a geas.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Others must choose
sb_spends.effect: It looks at the party; they must decide whether to pay the debt or abandon the breaker.

Herald Gargoyle (Dragon's Lair).summary: A living statue that enforces the dragon's etiquette, demanding a tithe before allowing passage.
Herald Gargoyle (Dragon's Lair).lore: The herald gargoyle was carved by the Aeler, but its soul was shaped by the dragon it serves. It does not attack—it judges. And its judgment is always final.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Demand the tithe
sb_spends.effect: It refuses passage until a suitable tribute is offered.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Seal the way
sb_spends.effect: It seals the passage until etiquette is satisfied.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Judge the offering
sb_spends.effect: It judges the quality of a tribute; a poor offering angers the dragon.

Fossil Juror (Dragon's Lair).summary: A sentient skeleton bound to judge intruders. It does not attack—it asks a riddle. Answer wrong, and you owe a geas.
Fossil Juror (Dragon's Lair).lore: The fossil juror was once a magistrate in a kingdom that fell to dust. Its judgment still holds, and its geasa are still binding.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Pose judgment
sb_spends.effect: It asks a riddle; wrong answer binds the PC to a geas.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Judgment timer
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Judgment' timer. At 4, it attacks the guilty.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Offer a verdict
sb_spends.effect: It allows a PC to condemn another to avoid the geas.

Ember Imp (Dragon's Lair).summary: A small, sharp-toothed creature that trades heat for secrets. It will light your lamp for a memory—and steal something when you aren't looking.
Ember Imp (Dragon's Lair).lore: The ember imp is a fragment of Azghal's Doomfire, given a shape and a hunger. It does not serve the dragon—it serves the heat, and it will barter with anyone who carries a spark.

sb_spends.name: [FIRE] Steal a spark
sb_spends.effect: It steals heat from a fire or lantern, extinguishing it.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Trade heat for secret
sb_spends.effect: It offers to light a way in exchange for a secret.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Pick a pocket
sb_spends.effect: It filches a small, flammable item.

Mirewing Basilisk-Drake (Dragon's Lair).summary: A venomous drake with a gaze that roots its prey in place. Haunts swampy zones and deep fens.
Mirewing Basilisk-Drake (Dragon's Lair).lore: The mirewing is a cousin to the true basilisk, but its gaze does not petrify—it binds. Those who meet its eyes feel the weight of the bog pulling them down.

sb_spends.name: [STONE] Binding gaze
sb_spends.effect: Its gaze roots a PC in place.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Bog claims the still
sb_spends.effect: A rooted PC begins to sink; start a 4-segment 'Sinking' timer.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Gaze holds
sb_spends.effect: Tick 'Binding' +1. At 4, the PC is fully immobilized.

Barrow Serpent (Dragon's Lair).summary: A serpent that dwells in burial mounds, feeding on the cold memory of the dead.
Barrow Serpent (Dragon's Lair).lore: The barrow serpent is a guardian of the dead, but it does not protect the living. It waits for warmth to enter the cold, and it coils around the careless.

sb_spends.name: [HAUNT] Taste the warmth
sb_spends.effect: It senses living warmth and targets the healthiest PC.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Barrow seals
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Barrow Seals' timer. At 4, the exit closes.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Dead stir
sb_spends.effect: The dead it guards rise to aid it.

Sky Serpent (Dragon's Lair).summary: A long, ribbon-like drake that nests in the highest peaks and hunts updrafts.
Sky Serpent (Dragon's Lair).lore: The sky serpent is the wind given form. It does not breathe fire—it breathes stillness, and those who catch its gaze find themselves falling.

sb_spends.name: [WIND] Breath of stillness
sb_spends.effect: It breathes stillness; a PC loses their footing and falls.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Ride the updraft
sb_spends.effect: It rides an updraft out of reach, forcing ranged combat.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] The sky turns
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Sky Falls' timer. At 4, a PC is dropped from a great height.

River Wight (Dragon's Lair).summary: A drowned spirit bound to a river, guarding a dragon's hoard or a sunken treasure.
River Wight (Dragon's Lair).lore: The river wight was once a guardian who drowned in the service of its wyrm. It cannot leave the water, but it can drown those who enter without permission.

sb_spends.name: [TIDE] Drown the intruder
sb_spends.effect: It drags a PC underwater; start a 4-segment 'Drowning' timer.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] River rises
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Flood' timer. At 4, the river claims the shore.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Ask permission
sb_spends.effect: It demands a tribute to allow passage across the water.

Hell Hound (Ember-Wolf).summary: A wolf of living fire, bound to the will of the Abyss. Hunts the lost and the damned.
Hell Hound (Ember-Wolf).lore: The hell hounds are the emissaries of the Abyss. They do not eat—they burn. They are not loyal—they are commanded.

sb_spends.name: [FIRE] Mark with flame
sb_spends.effect: Its bite sets a PC's gear smoldering.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Pack of embers
sb_spends.effect: More Hell Hounds arrive from a fissure of flame.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Hunt escalates
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Hunt' timer. At 4, they ignore all others and focus on a marked PC.

Stone-Eater.summary: A massive burrowing worm that tunnels through stone and earth. Its passage leaves no trace but the silence.
Stone-Eater.lore: The stone-eaters are the children of Nidhoggr, the corpse-tearer. They eat what the mountain leaves behind.

sb_spends.name: [ENVIRONMENT] Tunnel collapse
sb_spends.effect: Its passage collapses a tunnel behind or ahead of the party.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Swallow the path
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Devoured Path' timer. At 4, the only route is gone.

sb_spends.name: [PRESSURE] Silence before the worm
sb_spends.effect: All sound dies; the next attack is Dominant for the Stone-Eater.

Rakshasa (Masked Demon).summary: A demon of deception and pleasure, wearing the guise of nobility. Dwells in the courts of the powerful.
Rakshasa (Masked Demon).lore: The rakshasa are the demons of desire, feeding on the greed of the powerful. They are not summoned—they arrive, and they always have an invitation.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Twist the invitation
sb_spends.effect: It reveals the party was invited into a trap.

sb_spends.name: [BARGAIN] Offer corrupt power
sb_spends.effect: It offers a noble PC influence in exchange for a soul-debt.

sb_spends.name: [ILLUSION] Mask drops
sb_spends.effect: It briefly reveals its true form, terrifying all in Near.

Serpent-Folk.summary: A race of serpent-like beings, descended from the union of human and serpent spirit. Cold, calculating, and patient.
Serpent-Folk.lore: The serpent-folk are the children of the Serpent Queen. They remember the old empire and wait for its return—or they build their own, one convert at a time.

sb_spends.name: [SOCIAL] Offer conversion
sb_spends.effect: They offer a PC power if they swear to the Serpent Queen.

sb_spends.name: [TIMER] Venom takes hold
sb_spends.effect: Start a 4-segment 'Venom' timer. At 4, a bitten PC is dominated.

sb_spends.name: [REINFORCEMENT] Call the brood
sb_spends.effect: They summon more serpent-folk from hidden burrows.

Breath-Counting Ghost (Tier IV).summary: It does not attack. It counts. And when it reaches nine, you will remember what you forgot. A translucent figure in tattered Ykrul riding leathers, counting the breaths of the living. It appears at thresholds—doorways, bridges, and the space between waking and sleeping.
locations: The space between waking and sleeping
Breath-Counting Ghost (Tier IV).lore: The ghost is the echo of someone who died counting. In the Ykrul tradition, a rider who dies on the steppe without settling their debts is doomed to count forever. The ghost does not want to harm you. It wants you to remember.

sb_spends.name: Count of Eight
sb_spends.effect: The ghost counts your breaths aloud. For the rest of the scene, you suffer -1 die to all actions involving memory, promises, or navigation.

sb_spends.name: The Ninth Breath
sb_spends.effect: The ghost reaches nine. You remember a debt you owe. Mark 1 Obligation to the person you failed. If you have no outstanding debts, gain the 'Haunted by Possibility' condition—you dream of promises you haven't made yet.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Opens
sb_spends.effect: The ghost reveals a fragment of the reckoning of the region. You learn one true thing about a broken promise in this area—and one true thing about a promise that must be kept before the next full moon.

Oath-Keeper's Thorn (Tier IV).summary: A slender figure in a mask of woven hazel twigs, the Oath-Keeper's Thorn is a messenger of the Hazel Court. It appears when an oath is broken, a promise is forgotten, or a bargain is unpaid. It offers a choice: fulfill the oath, or pay the price.
Oath-Keeper's Thorn (Tier IV).lore: The Hazel Queen does not forgive. She renegotiates. The Thorn is her reminder that every promise is a root, and roots can be pulled up, or they can be watered. The choice is yours.

sb_spends.name: The Root Remembers
sb_spends.effect: The Thorn touches the ground; roots sprout from the soil, grasping at your ankles. You must test Resolve (DV 3) or be Rooted—unable to move until you fulfill or break the oath in question.

sb_spends.name: The Bargain Recalled
sb_spends.effect: The Thorn speaks the exact words of the broken oath aloud. All who hear it are Bound Witnesses; they cannot speak of the oath without also speaking of its breach. This imposes -1 die to all social rolls involving the oath until it is resolved.

sb_spends.name: The Hedge Grows
sb_spends.effect: The Thorn summons a barrier of thorny hazel between you and your objective. It requires a successful Body+Athletics test (DV 4) to pass through, and doing so causes 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Queen's Interest
sb_spends.effect: The Hazel Queen herself takes notice of the party. For the remainder of the session, all social rolls involving oaths, bargains, or hospitality are at -1 die. The Thorn gains +1 die to all actions against anyone who has broken an oath in its presence.

The Worn Captain (Tier V).summary: A gaunt figure in the tattered remains of a Black Banner captain's coat, the Worn Captain leads a squad of equally hollowed soldiers. He does not speak—his throat was cut by the collectors who came for what was owed. He communicates through gestures, each one a command that his soldiers obey without question.
The Worn Captain (Tier V).lore: The Worn Captain is a cautionary tale told in Black Banner camps: 'A captain who cannot count his paychest is a captain who will count his own grave.' He made a deal with a go-between in exchange for a season's worth of supplies. The go-between was not what they seemed. The deal was not a deal. And the interest is still mounting.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Weight
sb_spends.effect: The Captain draws his sword and taps it three times on the ground. All who hear it must test Resolve (DV 3) or feel the weight of their own unpaid debts. For the rest of the scene, any failure on a roll involving a promise or obligation generates an additional SB.

sb_spends.name: Form Up
sb_spends.effect: The Captain's soldiers form a shield wall. They cannot be bypassed without a successful Wits+Tactics test (DV 4); failure means you are forced to engage them directly.

sb_spends.name: The Unpaid Price
sb_spends.effect: One of the soldiers lunges forward, its rusted blade aimed at the character with the highest outstanding debt. The attack cannot be parried; it must be dodged (Body+Athletics, DV 4). On a hit, deal Harm 2 and mark 1 Obligation to the soldier's patron.

sb_spends.name: The Captain's Last Order
sb_spends.effect: The Captain points at a character. For the rest of the scene, that character hears a whisper in their ear: 'You will pay.' All of their social rolls are at -1 die, as the guilt of their debts distracts them.

sb_spends.name: Debt Called In
sb_spends.effect: The Captain names a character's greatest failure aloud. All witnesses hear the accusation. The character must test Spirit+Resolve (DV 4) or gain the 'Shamed' condition (-1 die to all Presence-based rolls until they publicly atone).

The Misstep (Tier V).summary: A shifting, uncertain shape that appears at the edge of perception—a stair that was not there, a door that should not open, a threshold that leads to the same room you just left. The Misstep is a reminder that some boundaries are not meant to be crossed.
The Misstep (Tier V).lore: In the Aelaerem tradition, the ninth step belongs to the Hollow. The Misstep is the Hollow's way of saying, 'You have mis-counted. Try again.' It is not a punishment. It is a correction.

sb_spends.name: The Threshold Shifts
sb_spends.effect: The Misstep rearranges the geometry of the current space. The party is separated by one room or corridor; you must spend an action to regroup.

sb_spends.name: The Ninth Step Recalled
sb_spends.effect: The Misstep shows you the moment when you (or someone you know) took a step that should not have been taken. The vision is vivid; you must test Resolve (DV 3) or lose a Boon.

sb_spends.name: The Door You Missed
sb_spends.effect: The Misstep reveals a door that was always there but never noticed. It leads to a location of the GM's choice—usually somewhere inconvenient, dangerous, or connected to an unresolved debt.

sb_spends.name: The Path That Loops
sb_spends.effect: The party finds themselves walking in circles. For the next exchange, any action that requires navigation is at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Hollow's Attention
sb_spends.effect: The Misstep's actions draw the Hollow's focus to the party. The Hollow's Attention timer advances by 2 segments. If there is no such timer, the GM gains 3 SB to spend on supernatural complications.

The Deep Warden (Tier VI).summary: A towering figure of stone and rusted iron, the Deep Warden patrols the forgotten vaults beneath the Aelerian mountains. It was not created—it accumulated, layer by layer, from the sediment of broken oaths and forgotten contracts. It does not speak. It does not negotiate. It enforces.
The Deep Warden (Tier VI).lore: The Deep Warden is not a servant of the Aeler. It is a consequence. When the Aeler built their vaults, they built them on the principle of 'enough.' But some debts are not paid. Some contracts are not fulfilled. The Deep Warden is the interest on those unpaid debts, made manifest.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: The Warden looks at a character. They feel their name being written onto the Warden's stone. For the rest of the scene, any action that involves breaking a promise or ignoring a contract is at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: Stone Grasps
sb_spends.effect: The Warden raises its hand; stone and rusted iron erupt from the ground, grasping at the party. Each character must test Body+Athletics (DV 3) or be Grappled; escaping requires a successful Body+Melee test (DV 4) as an action.

sb_spends.name: The Unpaid Clause
sb_spends.effect: The Warden cites a specific clause from a contract you have broken. You must test Resolve (DV 3) or mark 1 Obligation to the Aeler.

sb_spends.name: The Vault's Memory
sb_spends.effect: The Warden summons the ghost of a previous oath-breaker—a former adventurer who failed to fulfil their contract. The ghost attacks the party for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Interest mounts
sb_spends.effect: The Warden reaches into its chest and pulls out a fist-sized stone. It places it on the ground. The stone grows, becoming a smaller copy of the Warden that attacks the party independently.

sb_spends.name: The Contract's Final Clause
sb_spends.effect: The Warden demands a settlement. The party must offer something of value—a memory, a name, a year of service—or the Warden attacks with full force (+2 die to all its actions for the remainder of the scene).

Mist King's Herald (Tier VI).summary: A figure wrapped in fog, its face a mask of silvered mist, the Herald rides a horse made of fog and shadow. It appears when the Mistlands' bell-lines fail, riding from the Direwood to remind the living that some debts are older than the Mistlands themselves.
Mist King's Herald (Tier VI).lore: The Mist King's Herald is the echo of the first warden—the one who forgot to count the ninth bell. It rides the border between the Mistlands and the Direwood, carrying messages between the dead and the living. Sometimes the messages are warnings. Sometimes they are demands.

sb_spends.name: The Fog Thickens
sb_spends.effect: The Herald's presence causes fog to roll in. All ranged attacks are at -1 die for the scene, and navigation tests are at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The King's Command
sb_spends.effect: The Herald speaks a single word in the language of the Direwood. All who hear it must test Resolve (DV 3) or be Shaken (-1 die to all actions for one exchange).

sb_spends.name: The Bell Toll
sb_spends.effect: The Herald raises its hand; a bell tolls in the distance. The bell-line at the nearest village begins to fray; if not repaired within the scene, the Fog Attention timer advances by 2.

sb_spends.name: The Warden's Echo
sb_spends.effect: The Herald summons a wraith of a former warden—a figure in rusted Aeler armor that attacks the party. The wraith fights until destroyed or until the Herald is banished.

sb_spends.name: The Mist King's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: The Herald names a character's greatest failure—the moment they most disappointed someone they loved. The character must test Spirit+Resolve (DV 4) or be Wracked with Guilt (-2 dice to all actions until they atone).

sb_spends.name: The Direwood Opens
sb_spends.effect: The Herald creates a temporary path to the Direwood. Any character who follows it must test Resolve (DV 5) or become Lost in the Direwood, separated from the party.

Stone-Bound King (Tier VII).summary: A colossal figure carved from black granite, the Stone-Bound King sits on a throne of rubble in the deepest Aeler vaults. He was once a king who sought immortality. He found it—in the form of a mountain that would not let him go.
Stone-Bound King (Tier VII).lore: The Stone-Bound King was the last ruler of a kingdom that fell to the Aeler. He made a pact with the mountain: he would become stone, and in return, the mountain would protect his people. But the mountain did not distinguish between protection and imprisonment.

sb_spends.name: The Mountain's Weight
sb_spends.effect: The King's presence causes a tremor; all in the scene must test Body+Athletics (DV 3) or be Prone.

sb_spends.name: Stone Speaks
sb_spends.effect: The King's voice echoes through the stone. You hear it in your bones. All Resolve-based tests are at -1 die for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The King's Claim
sb_spends.effect: The King names a character as his heir. The character gains 1 Obligation to the King, and for the rest of the scene, all actions that involve claiming power or authority are at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Vault's Guardian
sb_spends.effect: The King summons a Stone Giant from the walls of the chamber. The Giant attacks the party until destroyed.

sb_spends.name: The Contract Recalled
sb_spends.effect: The King cites the exact terms of the pact he made with the mountain. You must test Lore (DV 5) to understand it; failure means you are Bound by the terms of a contract you did not knowingly sign.

sb_spends.name: The Mountain's Embrace
sb_spends.effect: The walls of the chamber begin to close in. Characters must test Body+Athletics (DV 5) or be Crushed (Harm 3). This effect continues for one exchange; after that, the King's power wanes.

sb_spends.name: The Unspoken Clause
sb_spends.effect: The King reveals a secret about the mountain that no one knows. The secret is true, and it is always a burden. The character who hears it gains 1 Obligation to the King.

Chained Angel's Echo (Tier VIII).summary: A figure of shadow and chains, the Chained Angel's Echo appears in places where debts have been called in and payments have been refused. She does not speak—her chains do. Each rattle is a word, each clink a clause, each groan a consequence.
Chained Angel's Echo (Tier VIII).lore: Malachai is the Chained Angel—a cosmic entity of obligation and consequence. The Echo is not Malachai herself, but a fragment of her will. It appears when debts have been called in and the one who owes has refused. The Echo does not bargain. It collects.
connections: The Daughters of the Unbroken Cord

sb_spends.name: The Chain's Weight
sb_spends.effect: The Echo rattles her chains. All in the scene must test Resolve (DV 3) or be Slowed (-1 die to all physical actions) for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Debt Named
sb_spends.effect: The Echo speaks the name of the debt you owe. You must test Spirit+Resolve (DV 4) or mark 1 Obligation immediately. If you have no outstanding debts, the Echo gains 1 SB for its next spend.

sb_spends.name: The Price of Freedom
sb_spends.effect: The Echo offers a terrible bargain: it will release one character from their debts, but another character must take on their burden. The character who accepts the bargain gains 3 Obligation.

sb_spends.name: The Chains Bind
sb_spends.effect: The Echo's chains reach out and wrap around a character. They are Grappled; escaping requires a successful Body+Melee test (DV 5) as an action.

sb_spends.name: The Interest mounts
sb_spends.effect: The Echo reveals that a debt you thought was settled is still mounting still. You must test Resolve (DV 4) or gain 2 Obligation to the person you thought you had paid.

sb_spends.name: The Echo of Malachai
sb_spends.effect: The Echo becomes momentarily indistinguishable from Malachai herself. All in the scene must test Spirit+Resolve (DV 5) or be Stunned (cannot act) for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Final Settlement
sb_spends.effect: The Echo offers one final bargain: it will forgive all debts of the party if one character agrees to become its vessel—to carry its chains until the debt is paid. The character who accepts gains 4 Obligation and becomes a target for future debt-collectors.

Hollow's Reckoning (Tier IX).summary: A manifestation of the Curse of Acasia—a debt collector of cosmic proportions. It appears when the Hollow's attention has been fully earned, and it does not leave until the debt is paid. It is a figure of gray mist and silence, and it has no face—only the shape of a face that once was.
Hollow's Reckoning (Tier IX).lore: The Hollow's Reckoning is the final stage of the Curse of Acasia. It is the consequence of a promise that was never kept, a debt that was never paid. It does not negotiate. It does not bargain. It collects—and it collects in full.

sb_spends.name: The Mist Thickens
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning's presence causes fog to roll in from nowhere. All actions that require sight are at -1 die for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Debt Spoken
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning speaks the name of the debt that has been called. All in the scene must test Resolve (DV 3) or be Shaken (-1 die to all actions for one exchange).

sb_spends.name: The Weight of Promises
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning creates a zone of oppressive silence. All social rolls in the scene are at -1 die, as the weight of unspoken promises presses down.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Opens
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning reveals the terms of the debt that has been called. The terms are always more severe than expected. Gain 2 Obligation to the Hollow.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Collects
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning causes a character to remember a debt they had forgotten. The character must test Resolve (DV 5) or mark 2 Obligation to the person they owe.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning looks at a character. That character gains 1 Obligation to the Hollow immediately, and for the rest of the scene, any action that involves making a promise is at -2 dice.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Touch
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning touches a character's forehead. The character loses access to one skill for 24 hours. The skill returns when the debt is paid.

Spear of the Forgotten Heroine (Tier IX).summary: A gilded spear of unknown origin, planted in the Alder Throne by a Linn heroine whose name was erased from history. It is not a weapon in the traditional sense—it is a witness, a memory, and a promise. Warm to the touch, as if it has been held recently.
Spear of the Forgotten Heroine (Tier IX).lore: The Spear was planted by a Linn heroine whose name was erased from history. She sealed the Mist King with the power of her true name, and then she went to the Alder Throne to plant the spear. She never returned. The spear holds her memory, her power, and her name—the name that can end the mist.

sb_spends.name: The Spear's Warmth
sb_spends.effect: The Spear glows faintly. All in the scene feel a sense of hope; gain +1 die to all Resolve-based rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Heroine's Voice
sb_spends.effect: The Spear whispers a fragment of the heroine's name. You must test Lore (DV 4) to remember it; success grants +1 die to all actions involving the Mist King for the rest of the scene. Failure means you lose the fragment.

sb_spends.name: The Gilded Light
sb_spends.effect: The Spear shines brightly, revealing hidden things. All investigations in the scene gain +1 die; illusions are automatically dispelled.

sb_spends.name: The Spear's Edge
sb_spends.effect: The Spear attacks a target of the GM's choice. Deal Harm 3, ignoring 2 armor. This attack cannot be used again in the same scene.

sb_spends.name: The Name Spoken
sb_spends.effect: A character speaks the heroine's name aloud. The Mist King's power wavers; all undead in the scene suffer -2 dice to all actions for the rest of the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Erased Wound
sb_spends.effect: The Spear's wielder may temporarily erase one wound—an injury, a disease, a curse. The character heals 2 Harm immediately, but the wound returns when the Spear is put down.

sb_spends.name: The Spear's Choice
sb_spends.effect: The Spear chooses a wielder. That character gains the power to end the Mist King's influence permanently—but they must take the Spear to the Alder Throne and speak the heroine's name there. The GM gains 4 SB to spend on complications along the way.

Unwritten King (Tier X).summary: A figure of shifting shadow and faint light, the Unwritten King appears at the edge of history—the moment before a kingdom is founded, the breath before a dynasty is born. He does not speak. He does not move. He is the king who never ruled, but whose rule is inevitable.
locations: The space between what was and what might have been
Unwritten King (Tier X).lore: The Unwritten King is the king who was never crowned—the ruler who was meant to unite the realm but was never born. He exists in the space between what was and what might have been. He is the personification of potential, and he is waiting for someone to claim the throne.

sb_spends.name: The Crown's Weight
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King's presence causes all in the scene to feel the weight of expectation. Gain 1 Fatigue to all characters.

sb_spends.name: The King's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King looks at a character. They feel the weight of a kingdom on their shoulders; all social rolls are at -1 die for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Throne's Claim
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King declares a character to be the heir to the kingdom of possibility. The character gains 1 Obligation to the Unwritten King, and for the rest of the campaign, they will face challenges related to leadership and responsibility.

sb_spends.name: The Unwritten Law
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King speaks a law that has never been spoken before. All in the scene must test Resolve (DV 4) or be Bound by the law (cannot act against it for the rest of the scene).

sb_spends.name: The Kingdom's Memory
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King summons a memory of a kingdom that never existed. All in the scene see it; they must test Resolve (DV 5) or be Distracted (-1 die to all actions) for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Crown's Choice
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King offers a character the chance to become the king of possibility—to rule over what might have been. The character who accepts gains 3 Obligation to the Unwritten King and the power to reshape one reality (GM's discretion).

sb_spends.name: The Inevitable Rule
sb_spends.effect: The Unwritten King declares that the party's actions have already been written in the book of what might have been. The party must accept that their choices are not choices—they are consequences. All actions in the scene are at -1 die, as the weight of inevitability presses down.

Bell-Warden's Shadow (Tier IV).summary: Every bell-warden has a shadow. The shadow is the part of them that remembers the tolls they have rung. A shadow that follows a bell-warden wherever they go, the Bell-Warden's Shadow is the manifestation of the tolls the warden has rung—the deaths, the warnings, the sealed doors.
Bell-Warden's Shadow (Tier IV).lore: The Shadow is the part of the bell-warden that remembers the silence after a bell is rung. It watches, patient and cold, waiting for the bell-warden to make a mistake.

sb_spends.name: The Unrung Bell
sb_spends.effect: The Shadow mimics the sound of a bell that was never rung. All in the scene must test Resolve (DV 3) or be Shaken (-1 die to all actions for one exchange).

sb_spends.name: The Toll Remembered
sb_spends.effect: The Shadow shows the bell-warden the face of a person they failed. The bell-warden gains 1 Obligation to the person's memory.

sb_spends.name: The Shadow's Claim
sb_spends.effect: The Shadow reaches out and touches a character. That character gains the 'Haunted by the Bell' condition—they hear bells in their sleep and are awakened by imaginary rings.

Salt-Eater (Tier V).summary: A creature made of crystallized salt and bone, the Salt-Eater feeds on the boundaries of the world. It appears at the edges of the Mistlands, where the wards are thin and the fog is hungry. It has no fixed shape—it is a shifting mass of salt crystals and bone fragments.
Salt-Eater (Tier V).lore: The Salt-Eater is a rare and dangerous entity that eats salt, eats wards, and eats the memory of boundaries. It is not malicious; it is hungry.

sb_spends.name: The Salt Line Breaks
sb_spends.effect: The Salt-Eater eats a line of salt, breaking a ward. The GM gains 1 SB to spend on supernatural complications.

sb_spends.name: The Crystallization
sb_spends.effect: The Salt-Eater sprays a cloud of salt crystals; all in Near range must test Body+Endurance (DV 4) or be Blinded for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Memory Eaten
sb_spends.effect: The Salt-Eater touches a character and eats a memory—a minor one, like the name of a street or the face of a stranger. The character cannot recall the memory until they perform a ritual of restoration.

Thornwood Rider (Tier VI).summary: A figure in rusted armor, mounted on a horse of woven thorn, the Thornwood Rider is a messenger of the Alder King. It appears when the Thornwood has been disturbed, and it does not leave until the wood is appeased.
locations: Where the wood has been disturbed
Thornwood Rider (Tier VI).lore: The Alder King's riders are not kind. They are precise. The Rider's face is a mask of woven thorn, its eyes two points of pale light. Its horse has no hooves—it moves on roots that burrow into the soil.

sb_spends.name: The Thorn's Grasp
sb_spends.effect: Roots erupt from the ground, grasping at a character. They must test Body+Athletics (DV 3) or be Grappled; escaping requires an action.

sb_spends.name: The Alder King's Claim
sb_spends.effect: The Rider declares a character to be a trespasser. The character gains 1 Obligation to the Alder King, and for the rest of the scene, all actions in natural terrain are at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Wood's Wrath
sb_spends.effect: The Rider summons a swarm of thorn-laden branches; all in Near range must test Resolve (DV 4) or take Harm 2.

sb_spends.name: The Rider's Challenge
sb_spends.effect: The Rider challenges a character to a duel. Refusing causes the character to be Marked by the Alder King (all Fey in the region will recognise them as a coward).

Mirror-Wraith (Tier VII).summary: A figure that exists only in reflections, the Mirror-Wraith preys on those who spend too long looking at themselves. It does not attack—it waits. And when you look away, it moves. It is visible only in reflections—a figure that stands behind you in a mirror, but vanishes when you turn around.
Mirror-Wraith (Tier VII).lore: The Mirror-Wraith lives in reflections. It waits for you to forget that mirrors show two sides. Its face is always slightly wrong, a distortion of your own features.

sb_spends.name: The Reflection Moves
sb_spends.effect: The Mirror-Wraith moves in a reflection, distracting a character. The character suffers -1 die to all actions for the exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Mirror's Claim
sb_spends.effect: The Mirror-Wraith reaches through a reflection and touches a character. They gain the 'Haunted by Reflections' condition—they see their own face in every mirror, and it is always slightly wrong.

sb_spends.name: The Reflected Self
sb_spends.effect: The Mirror-Wraith creates a duplicate of a character in a reflection. The duplicate attacks the character; it can only be defeated by destroying the mirror it is in.

sb_spends.name: The Unseen Gaze
sb_spends.effect: The Mirror-Wraith follows a character for the rest of the scene. They feel watched; all social rolls are at -1 die.

Iron Vow Keeper (Tier VIII).summary: A figure of rusted iron and glowing runes, the Iron Vow Keeper is a construct of ancient Aeler design. It was built to enforce the contracts of the mountain, but it has been waiting for so long that it has forgotten the terms. It keeps the vows that were never kept.
Iron Vow Keeper (Tier VIII).lore: The Keeper has no face—only a smooth, polished surface. Its body is covered in runes that glow with a soft, red light. Its voice is the sound of a bell that has been struck and then held, the note lingering impossibly long.

sb_spends.name: The Vow Recalled
sb_spends.effect: The Keeper speaks a vow that has been broken. All who hear it must test Resolve (DV 3) or mark 1 Obligation to the Keeper.

sb_spends.name: The Iron Grasp
sb_spends.effect: The Keeper's hand closes on a character. They must test Body+Melee (DV 4) or be Grappled; escaping requires a successful test.

sb_spends.name: The Contract's Weight
sb_spends.effect: The Keeper reveals a clause in the original vow that has not been fulfilled. The character must test Lore (DV 5) to understand it; failure means they are Bound by the terms of a contract they cannot break.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Collects
sb_spends.effect: The Keeper's presence causes all debts in the scene to become visible—everyone knows exactly what everyone else owes. All social rolls are at -1 die for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Unpaid Price
sb_spends.effect: The Keeper demands payment. The party must offer something of value—a memory, a name, a year of service—or the Keeper attacks with full force (+2 die to all its actions for the remainder of the scene).

summary: An archivist who discovered a sealed file containing the truth of a noble's death. The Witness showed them what was in the file. Now they cannot stop reading—every record, every contract, every hidden clause.
lore: They seek to expose the truth, but the truth has exposed them first.

sb_spends.name: Reveal the Hidden Clause
sb_spends.effect: The Aspirant points out a detail everyone missed; one character's next Investigation roll gains +1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Unbearable Truth
sb_spends.effect: They speak a painful truth aloud; one character must test Resolve (DV 3) or mark 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Witness's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: They reveal a secret about the party; the GM gains 2 SB to spend on complications related to that secret.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — a mortal follower, not the power they serve.

summary: A former courtier who was exiled for speaking the truth about a noble's adultery. They carry a silver mirror everywhere, seeking faces that cannot hide.
lore: They are kind, and they are terrifying.

sb_spends.name: The Silver Mirror
sb_spends.effect: They show a character their reflection; the character sees the truth of their own heart and gains +1 die to resist emotional manipulation for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Unmasked Face
sb_spends.effect: They force a target to look into the mirror; the target must test Resolve (DV 4) or reveal a hidden motive.

sb_spends.name: The Witness's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: They declare a character's actions have been witnessed; all of that character's social rolls are at -1 die for the scene.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — a mortal follower, not the power they serve.

summary: A scholar who found a sealed tomb and opened it, discovering evidence of a crime the empire wished to forget. The Witness showed them the truth.
lore: Now they seek more truth, and they will not stop until they find the name of the architect who built the First City.

sb_spends.name: The Unsealed Door
sb_spends.effect: They have a key; unlock any one mundane lock or seal.

sb_spends.name: The Found Truth
sb_spends.effect: They reveal a clue the party missed; gain +1 die on the next Investigation roll.

sb_spends.name: The Lost Name
sb_spends.effect: They recall a name that has been erased from history; the GM must answer one truthfully about the person or place named.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — a mortal follower, not the power they serve.

summary: A former gladiator who won their freedom by killing a prince in the arena. They carry the prince's broken chain as a talisman.
lore: They believe that the only law is the one you enforce with your own hands.

sb_spends.name: Chain's Memory
sb_spends.effect: They show a character the broken chain; the character sees a vision of their own oppression and gains +1 die to resist coercion for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Unstoppable Charge
sb_spends.effect: They move with impossible speed; one character who opposes them is knocked Prone.

sb_spends.name: The Riven Path Opens

sb_spends.name: The Optimization's Touch
sb_spends.effect: They touch a character; the character gains +1 die to all actions for the scene, but marks 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Iteration's Claim
sb_spends.effect: They improve a character's skill; the character gains +1 die to one skill permanently, but marks 2 Obligation.

sb_spends.name: The Perfection's Price
sb_spends.effect: They offer a character perfection; the character gains +2 dice to all actions for the scene, but marks 2 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Monad's Demand
sb_spends.effect: They demand an improvement; a character must improve something or suffer Harm 2.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A floating eye of silver and light, the Witness's Eye is the embodiment of the Witness's power. It does not speak—it observes.
lore: And when it observes, it sees everything.

sb_spends.name: The Eye's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: It looks at a character; the character is Seen (cannot hide or lie for the scene).

sb_spends.name: The Eye's Memory
sb_spends.effect: It recalls a truth; the GM must answer one question truthfully.

sb_spends.name: The Eye's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: It names a lie; the liar suffers -1 die to all actions for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Eye's Revelation
sb_spends.effect: It reveals a secret; the GM must reveal a hidden truth about the scene.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A path that appears where none was before, the Traveler's Road is the embodiment of the Traveler's power. It does not speak—it guides.
lore: And where it leads, you will follow.

sb_spends.name: The Road's Claim
sb_spends.effect: It appears; a character must follow or suffer -1 die to all actions.

sb_spends.name: The Road's Memory
sb_spends.effect: It remembers a path; a character gains +1 die to all Navigation rolls.

sb_spends.name: The Road's Gift
sb_spends.effect: It offers a shortcut; a character reaches their destination in half the time, but marks 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Road's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: It declares a path closed; a character cannot travel along that route for the scene.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A massive door of black iron, the Sentinel's Seal is the embodiment of the Sealed Gate's power. It does not speak—it bars.
lore: And what it bars, cannot pass.

sb_spends.name: The Seal's Claim
sb_spends.effect: It closes a door; a character cannot pass through for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Seal's Memory
sb_spends.effect: It remembers a threshold; a character gains +1 die to all Defense rolls.

sb_spends.name: The Seal's Gift
sb_spends.effect: It offers protection; a character gains +1 Armor for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Seal's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: It declares a boundary; a character cannot cross the boundary for the scene.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A figure of living ivy and wild laughter, the Lord of Revels is the embodiment of Thrysos's power—the ecstasy, the frenzy, the abandon.
lore: They are the dance that never ends.

sb_spends.name: The Dance's Claim
sb_spends.effect: They begin to dance; all characters must test Resolve (DV 5) or be drawn into the dance.

sb_spends.name: The Revel's Gift
sb_spends.effect: They offer a character a sip of sacred wine; the character gains +2 dice to all actions for the scene, but marks 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Madness of the Revel
sb_spends.effect: They unleash the wild celebration; all characters act at Desperate Position for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: The Revel's Price
sb_spends.effect: They demand a sacrifice; a character must offer something of value—a memory, a name, a year of service—or suffer Harm 4.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A figure of shadow and chains, the Chained Angel's Embrace is the embodiment of Malachai's power—the curse, the bargain, the price.
lore: They are patient, and they have all the time in the world.

sb_spends.name: The Chain's Claim
sb_spends.effect: They speak a word of binding; all characters must test Resolve (DV 5) or be Slowed.

sb_spends.name: The Curse's Gift
sb_spends.effect: They offer a character a cursed gift; the character gains +2 dice to all actions for the scene, but marks 2 Obligation.

sb_spends.name: The Curse's Price
sb_spends.effect: They demand a sacrifice; a character must offer something of value—a memory, a name, a future—or suffer Harm 4.

sb_spends.name: The Chained Angel's Bargain
sb_spends.effect: They offer a character a deal; the character is freed from one obligation but gains 3 Obligation to Malachai.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.

summary: A figure of ash and ember, the Unmaker's Flame is the embodiment of Mor'iraath's power—the fire, the erasure, the finality.
lore: They are the flame that leaves no trace.

sb_spends.name: The Fire's Claim
sb_spends.effect: They speak a word of fire; all characters suffer Harm 1 (Burn).

sb_spends.name: The Unmaker's Gift
sb_spends.effect: They offer a character the gift of oblivion; the character is freed from one obligation, but loses a memory.

sb_spends.name: The Unmaker's Price
sb_spends.effect: They demand a sacrifice; a character must offer something of value—a memory, a name, a future—or suffer Harm 4.

sb_spends.name: The Absolute Ending
sb_spends.effect: They name a thing that should not exist; the thing ceases to exist for the scene.

summary: A pragmatic mine foreman who has lost too many miners to superstition. He wants to blast the tunnel where the lamplighter died.
lore: He is not cruel—he is exhausted. His patience is running out.

sb_spends.name: The Foreman's Patience
sb_spends.effect: He offers a warning; a character gains +1 die to avoid danger.

sb_spends.name: The Foreman's Wrath
sb_spends.effect: He loses his temper; a character suffers -1 die to all social rolls with him for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Foreman's Decision
sb_spends.effect: He decides to blast the tunnel; the party must act quickly or lose the opportunity.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: An old woman who remembers her husband's face—but only barely. She is the only one who can break the Echo.
lore: Her memory is fading, and she is terrified of forgetting.

sb_spends.name: The Widow's Memory
sb_spends.effect: She recalls a detail; the GM must answer one question about the lamplighter's death.

sb_spends.name: The Widow's Grief
sb_spends.effect: She weeps; all characters suffer -1 die to all actions for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Widow's Decision
sb_spends.effect: She agrees to speak her husband's name; the Echo is broken.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A Sidhi dock-master who has been paying the mother of a ghoul to keep her quiet. He wants the ghoul dealt with quietly—permanently.
lore: He does not want the Admiralty involved.

sb_spends.name: The Dock-Master's Patience
sb_spends.effect: He offers a bribe; a character gains +1 die to all social rolls with him for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Dock-Master's Wrath
sb_spends.effect: He loses his temper; a character suffers -1 die to all social rolls with him for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Dock-Master's Decision
sb_spends.effect: He demands action; the party must deal with the ghoul or lose his trust.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A young Sidhi woman who was cursed after drinking from a contaminated well. She does not want to kill—she is starving.
lore: She remembers her mother's face. She does not want to forget.

sb_spends.name: The Ghoul's Hunger
sb_spends.effect: She begs for food; a character must offer something or she becomes hostile.

sb_spends.name: The Ghoul's Memory
sb_spends.effect: She recalls her mother's face; a character must test Resolve (DV 4) or be moved to pity.

sb_spends.name: The Ghoul's Decision
sb_spends.effect: She chooses to feed; the party must either stop her or accept the consequences.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A fourteen-year-old girl who has been possessed by a demon. She speaks in languages she never learned. The Inquisition plans to burn her.
lore: She is terrified, and she is not the demon.

sb_spends.name: The Girl's Fear
sb_spends.effect: She begs for help; a character must test Resolve (DV 4) or be moved to act.

sb_spends.name: The Demon's Voice
sb_spends.effect: It speaks through her; a character suffers -1 die to all actions for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Girl's Decision
sb_spends.effect: She chooses to trust the party; the party gains the opportunity to perform an exorcism.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A fungal-warden who tends the mycelial networks of the Deepwood. She serves the Carrion King, tending the dead and the dying.
lore: She is patient, kind, and she has seen the cycle of life and death play out a thousand times.

sb_spends.name: The Warden's Wisdom
sb_spends.effect: She offers advice; a character gains +1 die to all Lore rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Warden's Gift
sb_spends.effect: She offers a fungal medicine; a character heals 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: The Warden's Demand
sb_spends.effect: She asks for a sacrifice; a character must offer something to the soil or suffer the consequences.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A man who weighs grain and judges contracts. He has never believed in anything except what was owed. His daughter is possessed.
lore: He refuses to help. He is guilty, and he knows it.

sb_spends.name: The Censor's Guilt
sb_spends.effect: He offers a bribe; a character gains +1 die to all social rolls with him for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Censor's Secret
sb_spends.effect: He reveals a hidden contract; a character gains +1 die to all Investigation rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Censor's Decision
sb_spends.effect: He confesses; the party gains the information they need to save his daughter.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A Sidhi woman who knows what her daughter has become—and still loves her. She leaves bowls of animal blood at the sewer entrance.
lore: She has not given up, and she never will.

sb_spends.name: The Mother's Love
sb_spends.effect: She pleads for mercy; a character must test Resolve (DV 4) or be moved to act.

sb_spends.name: The Mother's Hope
sb_spends.effect: She offers a token of her daughter; a character gains +1 die to all social rolls with Zel for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Mother's Decision
sb_spends.effect: She chooses to trust the party; the party gains the opportunity to save her daughter.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A nameless traveler who has walked every road in the Amaranthine. They know the secrets of the Patrons, the ways of the Hollow, and the names of the forgotten.
lore: They offer advice—and they always ask for a story in return.

sb_spends.name: The Wanderer's Wisdom
sb_spends.effect: They offer a piece of advice; a character gains +1 die to all Lore rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Wanderer's Memory
sb_spends.effect: They recall a forgotten name; a character gains +1 die to all social rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Wanderer's Demand
sb_spends.effect: They ask for a story; a character must share a secret or lose the Wanderer's trust.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A legendary thief who is said to have stolen a coin from the Hollow's own pocket. She is a folk hero to the downtrodden, a cautionary tale to the rich.
lore: She is beautiful, and she is dangerous. She owes debts to everyone—and no one.

sb_spends.name: The Velvet Touch
sb_spends.effect: She steals something without being noticed; a character loses a Boon.

sb_spends.name: The Serafine's Secret
sb_spends.effect: She reveals a secret about a mark; a character gains +1 die to all Deception rolls for the scene.

sb_spends.name: The Serafine's Demand
sb_spends.effect: She asks for a favor; a character must perform a task for her or lose her trust.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: The faceless head of the Inquisition, a figure of absolute purity and judgment. They are not a person—they are a will.
lore: They hunt the heretical and the corrupt, and they never show mercy.

sb_spends.name: The Inquisitor's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: They look at a character; the character is Judged (cannot hide from the Inquisition for the scene).

sb_spends.name: The Inquisitor's Demand
sb_spends.effect: They ask for a confession; a character must confess to a crime or be marked as guilty.

sb_spends.name: The Inquisitor's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: They declare a character guilty; the character is hunted by the Inquisition for the scene.

harm_levels: 3 (standard) — an ordinary mortal, not built for combat.

summary: A figure of woven hazel, the Oath-Keeper is the embodiment of the Hazel Court's power—the arbiter of promises, the collector of debts, the guardian of the old ways.
lore: They are patient, and they do not forgive.

sb_spends.name: The Oath-Keeper's Claim
sb_spends.effect: They name a broken oath; the oath-breaker gains 1 Obligation.

sb_spends.name: The Oath-Keeper's Demand
sb_spends.effect: They ask for a promise; a character must swear an oath or be marked as untrustworthy.

sb_spends.name: The Oath-Keeper's Judgment
sb_spends.effect: They declare a debt unpaid; the one who owes suffers -1 die to all social rolls for the scene.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — a puzzle of payment and confession, not a fight.

summary: A manifestation of the Curse of Acasia—a debt collector of cosmic proportions. It appears when the Hollow's attention has been fully earned.
lore: It is a figure of gray mist and silence, and it has no face—only the shape of a face that once was.

sb_spends.name: The Mist Thickens
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning's presence causes fog to roll in; all actions that require sight are at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Debt Spoken
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning speaks the name of the debt that has been called; all characters must test Resolve (DV 4) or be Shaken.

sb_spends.name: The Weight of Promises
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning creates a zone of oppressive silence; all social rolls are at -1 die.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Opens
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning reveals the terms of the debt; the terms are always more severe than expected. Gain 2 Obligation to the Hollow.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning Collects
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning causes a character to remember a debt they had forgotten; the character gains 2 Obligation.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Gaze
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning looks at a character; the character gains 1 Obligation to the Hollow and suffers -1 die to all actions involving promises.

sb_spends.name: The Reckoning's Touch
sb_spends.effect: The Reckoning touches a character's forehead; the character loses access to one skill for 24 hours.

harm_levels: None. Unkillable — Avatars are puzzles to solve (a name, a bargain, a rite), never fights to win by attrition.
